title: SPA fallback can serve files outside the frontend directory
reasoning: The catch-all route treats the user-controlled path parameter as a filesystem path without resolving it back under FRONTEND_DIR. A request containing encoded parent-directory segments can make file_path point outside the built frontend tree, and FileResponse will serve any readable file that exists. Because this route is network-exposed when the frontend build is present, this can disclose source files or host/container files.
reproduction: With the frontend build enabled, request a path such as GET /%2e%2e/app/main.py or GET /%2e%2e/%2e%2e/etc/passwd using a client that does not normalize the path before sending it.
recommendation: Resolve both FRONTEND_DIR and the candidate path, then only serve direct files whose resolved path is inside the resolved frontend directory. Reject traversal attempts with a real 404, or serve static files through Starlette StaticFiles which already performs containment checks.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The discovered tests import the app without a frontend/index.html build artifact, so serve_spa is not registered. No linked test exercises direct file serving through the catch-all route with encoded traversal input.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a temporary frontend build fixture, register/import the app with that build present, then assert GET /%2e%2e/app/main.py returns 404 and does not contain source text while a legitimate frontend asset still returns 200.
minimumFixScope: Constrain the direct-file branch in serve_spa to resolved paths under FRONTEND_DIR.
